texts: An extracardiac Fontan is not performed during an anatomic biventricular repair: E.
The anatomic ("double switch") repair restores the morphological left ventricle to the systemic circulation by combining an atrial switch (Senning or Mustard) with an arterial switch.
With a VSD and pulmonary stenosis, the arterial switch is replaced by a Rastelli-type tunnel from the left ventricle to the aorta and a conduit.
A bidirectional Glenn is often added to unload a small right ventricle or the atrial baffle (a hemi-Mustard).
A Fontan is a single-ventricle route, the opposite of a biventricular repair.
In the picture, the mustard, the lever, the tunnel and the astronaut all work, while the fountain stays covered.
Memory hook: a double switch needs mustard and a lever, never a fountain.
